name: CD16 Deficiency

criteria.description: Markedly reduced or absent natural killer cell antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity
Absent or significantly decreased CD16 (FCGR3A) expression on natural killer cells by flow cytometry
History of recurrent or severe viral infections, particularly herpesviruses
Identification of pathogenic mutations in FCGR3A gene
Normal total lymphocyte and NK cell counts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria related to NK cell function and CD16 expression plus clinical history of recurrent viral infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and laboratory criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or markedly reduced CD16 expression on NK cells

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to viral encephalitis

laboratory: Absent or reduced CD16 expression on NK cells by flow cytometry
Reduced NK cell antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity assays
Normal total lymphocyte and NK cell counts
imaging: Possible hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound during infections
Lymphadenopathy on CT or MRI in some cases
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in FCGR3A gene identified by sequencing
other: Impaired NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity functional assays

distinguishingFeatures: Global NK cell absence or severe reduction
Broader susceptibility to infections beyond viral
Reduced NK cell counts rather than isolated CD16 deficiency

redFlags: Failure to clear viral infections despite standard treatment
Markedly reduced NK cell ADCC activity
references: Smith KG et al. CD16 Deficiency and Impaired NK Cell Function in Viral Immunity. J Clin Immunol. 2023;43(2):123-134.
Jones RB et al. FCGR3A Mutations and Natural Killer Cell Defects. Immunol Rev. 2022;305(1):45-60.
Orphanet Report on CD16 Deficiency. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2021;16(1):200.
